title: College football coaching carousel 2026: Tracking all the changes so far - CBS Sports
description: Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
body:
Get the latest on the college football coaching carousel as CBS Sports tracks new hires and fires
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a few false starts, the coaching carousel finally started spinning in late October.It's not surprising the silly season is off to a slow start after 2025's record-breaking churn. The FBS hired 32 new head coaches, including 17 in the four power conferences, and hundreds more assistant coaches changed jobs.Ninety-three FBS programs have changed coaches over the last three offseasons. The question is whether we've hit a cooling period as schools wrestle with the challenging economics of the NIL and revenue-sharing era. Maryland kicked off the firing season Oct. 21. More power programs have followed. CBS Sports is tracking every move in the 2026-27 cycle and grading each hire below.
Power Four
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baylor — OUT: Dave Aranda | IN: TBDDave Aranda won a Big 12 title in 2021 but otherwise led the Bears with middling success over seven seasons. He finished 40-40 and was below .500 in the Big 12 (26-32). Don't be surprised if Baylor seeks an offensive coach, particularly one with strong connections to the Texas high school scene. UTSA's Jeff Traylor, Texas State's GJ Kinne and USC's Lincoln Riley are strong candidates to consider in Waco.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Florida State — OUT: Mike Norvell | IN: TBDAfter seven whirlwind seasons, which included an undefeated campaign in 2023 while being snubbed from the College Football Playoff, Florida State cut ties with Norvell on Nov. 1 following a loss to Clemson. Is FSU as lucrative a job as it has been in the past? We'll find out as questions arise about the program's financials. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Maryland — OUT: Mike Locksley | IN: TBDMaryland kicked off the coaching carousel this year. Mike Locksley is out halfway through his eighth season at Maryland, where he was 39-54 overall. The Terps were 4-8 in back-to-back seasons leading to the decisive 2026. A wide variety of candidates will be considered in College Park. Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, a popular name elsewhere, and Memphis' Charles Huff, a Maryland native, immediately come to mind. Dickert, however, recently signed a new contract with Wake. The Terps have better NIL resources than a year ago, but the job is still difficult in the Big Ten.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State — OUT: Dave Doeren | IN: Philip RiversNC State legend Philip Rivers was hired to lead his former program to the mountaintop of the ACC. The legendary NFL quarterback spent six years coaching St. Michael's Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama, where he led the program to the playoffs four times. His son, Gunner, is a quarterback committed to NC State. With only a $3.5 million annual salary, NC State is counting on fans and boosters to help fund NIL and secure an elite roster. Dave Doeren was fired during his 14th season in Raleigh, following a disappointing 31-28 loss at Stanford that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC. Doeren seemed just good enough to win seven to nine games every year, but disappointing losses always railroaded what could have been special seasons. A downtick in success over the last three years made it clear a change was needed.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    UTEP — OUT: Scotty Walden | IN: TBDScotty Walden is out after a 1-9 start in his third season leading UTEP. His tenure produced only six wins across three seasons and the nation's worst-scoring offense in 2026. The Miners' athletics program is among the worst-funded in the country, making this job incredibly challenging. Remember, Walden was coaching at FCS Austin Peay before coming to El Paso, so the list of candidates this time around could be shallow.

title: The lost years of Lamar Jackson: How injuries have interrupted his prime - CBS Sports
description: Some years, Lamar Jackson's thumb hits another player and is fine. Some years, his ankle just gets hit rather than rolled up on. And tho
body:
Some years, Lamar Jackson's thumb hits another player and is fine. Some years, his ankle just gets hit rather than rolled up on. And those years, he has been -- and will be -- a player who can win an MVP and perhaps a Super Bowl.It has not been one of those years.Jackson's latest injury was almost too cruel to believe. After missing the previous three and a half games with a high ankle sprain, the two-time MVP was finally back. So, too, was the Ravens' hope. Jackson had looked phenomenal -- MVP-level phenomenal -- in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system. Not only was he back, but he was back in a big spot: against fellow MVP Josh Allen in a crucial matchup vs. Buffalo on the first day of November, with Baltimore trying to end a two-game losing streak.And then, on the Ravens' first play, Jackson hit his thumb on Greg Rousseau's arm. Jackson looked down at his injured right thumb, trotted toward the sideline and then took a knee."Oh boy," NFL on CBS analyst Ross Tucker said.Medical personnel surrounded Jackson, draped a towel over his hand and brought him down the tunnel, off the field.
"Oh my goodness," Tucker said.What more was there to say? Lamar Jackson, one of the defining players not just of the era but of NFL history, was hurt. Again. And it was serious. Again.Jackson officially landed on IR with a thumb injury that will require surgery. It is "potentially" season-ending, and with the Ravens 4-5 and losers of four straight, it's looking like a lost season in Baltimore. This is the fourth time in the last six years the 29-year-old has missed at least four games. It has robbed the Ravens of their Super Bowl aspirations. It has robbed the NFL of a superstar. And it has robbed Jackson, a Heisman Trophy winner and twice an NFL MVP, of even higher levels of all-time greatness.Lamar Jackson's injury historyOn the positive side, the thumb injury is the first ailment to land Jackson on IR. He has never had an ACL tear, an Achilles tear, etc. On the negative side, Jackson has racked up so many injuries of so many different kinds that it seems like something is constantly getting in the way, whether it's nagging at him or keeping him out of games. He even said the ankle pain entering the Bills game last week was merely "bearable," not gone.
Since the start of last season alone, Jackson has had hamstring, ankle, toe, knee, back, and thumb ailments. Not all of those kept him out, but they add up. He admitted he came back from last year's hamstring injury too early, impacting his play all season.Lamar Jackson's NFL injuriesGames missedNov. 2026ThumbTBD (at least 4)Oct. 2026High ankle sprain3Dec. 2025Tailbone bruise1Sept. 2025Right hamstring strain3Dec. 2022Left PCL (knee) sprain6, incl. wild card gameDec. 2021Right ankle sprain4And yes, for what it's worth, it's bad luck. If Jackson's hand hits Rousseau at any other angle, he might not hurt his thumb enough to need surgery. If a diving Jermaine Johnson II doesn't awkwardly trap Jackson's ankle to the turf in Week 3, Jackson might not miss the next three games. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes have both had hundreds of similar plays and, with the exception of Mahomes' torn ACL last year, avoided injury for the most part. Sometimes, it's simply human anatomy, something Jackson cannot change.For as prolific a runner as Jackson is, he does an excellent job avoiding hits on those plays. None of his injuries have been on runs. It has just been a constant parade of misfortune. Unfortunately for Jackson and the Ravens, the NFL rolls on, whether you're lucky or not.
The cost of Jackson's injuries: individual greatnessPerhaps time and injuries have taken their toll and blocked our collective memory from how incredible Jackson has been. That would be truly unfortunate.In 2019, Jackson's second year of the league, he threw 36 touchdown passes and ran for 1,206 yards. In NFL history, there are ...356 individual seasons of 1,200+ rushing yards162 individual seasons of 30+ passing touchdownsThere is ONE with both: Jackson in 2019.In fact, only one other player ever has posted 1,200 rushing yards and merely double-digit passing touchdowns in a season: Spec Sanders of the New York Yankees (football version) in the All-America Football Conference in 1947. But he only threw 14 touchdowns. Jackson did things modern football has never known.
Jackson became the youngest quarterback to win MVP and joined Tom Brady as the only unanimous MVPs in NFL history. There are many ways to measure individual season greatness, but Pro Football Reference's "Approximate Value" is as good as any. Jackson had an approximate value of 25 in 2019, tied for the second-best season on record; LaDanian Tomlinson's 2006 season, in which he scored an NFL-record 31 touchdowns, is the only one better.Jackson was healthy in 2020 and had another strong season, including a second straight 1,000-yard rushing effort. He has as many 1,000-yard rushing seasons as all other quarterbacks in NFL history combined (Michael Vick and Justin Fields both have one).Then the injuries started. In 2021, Jackson was on pace for another 1,000-yard rushing season, and the Ravens led the AFC North when Browns linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah dove at Jackson's ankles after Jackson released a pass. Jackson got carted off and didn't play in any of the final four games. The Ravens lost all four and missed the playoffs.
The next year, Jackson sprained his PCL when his left knee got driven into the ground on a sack by the Broncos' Jonathan Cooper. He ended up missing six weeks -- the final five of the regular season and a wild card game, which Baltimore lost.This was a strange one. John Harbaugh initially wondered if Jackson could be back the next week and added "If not, it'll be sometime after that shortly." Then, Ravens officials were confident Jackson would return for the playoffs, per ESPN, leaving Jackson to essentially rule himself out -- and give his own medical update -- via social media.In 2023, though, Jackson was healthy and marvelous once again. Under new offensive coordinator Todd Monken, Jackson set career highs in completion percentage (67.2%), passing yards (3,678) and yards per attempt (8.0). He was still excellent on the ground with a team-high 821 yards. He won MVP and was one vote short of doing so unanimously.
Jackson's glorious 2023 season earned him his second Most Valuable Player award.  
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            He was somehow even better in 2024, with 4,172 passing yards and 8.8 yards per attempt. He threw 41 touchdowns and just four interceptions. He ran for 915 yards. He had already reached unprecedented levels. Now, he was reaching new ones, as the first player with:4,000 or more passing yards and 600 or more rushing yards40 or more passing touchdowns and 800 or more rushing yards40 or more passing touchdowns and fewer than five interceptionsHis 10.25 touchdown-to-interception ratio was also the best ever in any 30-touchdown season.Somehow Jackson didn't win MVP. He was a first-team All-Pro, but MVP went to Allen, an extreme rarity. Jackson would have been the youngest three-time MVP in NFL history. That's how good the start was.
From 2019 to 2024, Jackson ranked third in passer rating and touchdown-to-interception ratio and fourth in yards per attempt. He was also fourth in touchdown passes despite missing significant time in two seasons. He was also eighth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry.He was the Shohei Ohtani of football. No one can be this good at two different aspects, right? Wrong. Jackson was truly exceptional, and he seemed to be getting better.He had nine touchdowns and zero interceptions on an absurd 9.6 yards per attempt through three weeks of 2025. Then came the hamstring injury, which started an avalanche of injuries. The hits haven't stopped coming since.
The cost of Jackson's injuries: missed playoff chancesIf two things stand out as Jackson's career shortcomings, it's injuries and playoff performance. The two are somewhat intertwined. In 2021, Baltimore missed the playoffs. In 2022, Jackson missed the playoffs. Last year, his injuries derailed the Ravens, but they somehow got a Week 18 win-and-in game against the Steelers. Tyler Loop missed a game-winning field goal attempt. It's looking like he will not add to his postseason ledger this season, either.Had Jackson been healthy in even two of those four lost seasons, is he a Super Bowl champ? Or does he at least have more postseason wins?Jackson is one of nine quarterbacks to win multiple MVP awards since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. Of those nine, Jackson has the second-fewest playoff wins (two) before his 30th birthday, only ahead of the famously late-blooming Steve Young. 
Wins, it is said, are not a quarterback stat, and that can be true. Unfortunately for Jackson and the Ravens, both his play and his team's have declined in the postseason. The Ravens are 3-6 in the playoffs since drafting Jackson in 2018 (3-5 with Jackson as the starter).Jackson lost in his playoff debut in 2018, but the real disappointment came after his 2019 NFL season. With the Ravens as the AFC No. 1 seed, he had 365 yards and a touchdown passing and 143 yards rushing against the Titans, but he also had two interceptions,  lost a fumble, and failed on two fourth-and-short runs.The next year, Jackson earned his first playoff win, getting a measure of revenge on the Titans in the wild card round. But one week later, Baltimore went quietly in a 17-3 loss to Buffalo, most remembered for Jackson throwing a terrible end-zone interception that Taron Johnson returned 101 yards for a touchdown.
Jackson suffered a concussion on the final play of the third quarter and did not return.His next playoff game came after his 2023 MVP campaign. He was excellent in a win over the Texans, but in the AFC Championship, he lost a fumble and had another awful end-zone interception, this time in the fourth quarter. The Chiefs won 17-10, and Jackson's two turnovers loomed large.In 2024, the Ravens, supercharged by the Derrick Henry addition, were on the precipice of a return to the AFC Championship Game before falling to the Bills, 27-25. Jackson again had turnover issues -- a bad interception and an even worse fumble, the latter of which led the a Buffalo touchdown -- but that game is better remembered for a Mark Andrews fumble and, later, drop on the potential game-tying two-point attempt.There have been tons of moments where supporting cast members have let Jackson down in crucial moments. Andrews' nightmare two seasons ago and Zay Flowers' fumble at the 1-yard line against the Chiefs certainly come to mind. There's a lack of game-changing plays from the defense: two turnovers forced in Jackson's seven postseason starts, and none in the past two playoff trips, when hopes were the highest. But it's undeniable that Jackson has been very poor in the playoffs, too.Lamar Jackson careerReg. seasonPlayoffsPlayoff rank (out of 26)<<TD/Int3.41.420thNet yards per attempt7.56.515thEPA per dropback0.13-0.0120thTurnovers per game0.721.3822nd>> Min. 3 playoff starts since 2018The final stat -- turnovers -- is truly staggering ... and costly. Jackson's turnovers have cost the Ravens an estimated 6.86 points per game in the playoffs, basically a touchdown. The only quarterbacks with a higher rate out of the 26-player sample are Drake Maye, Justin Herbert, and Trevor Lawrence.Unless there's a major turnaround, this stands to be the Jackson's fourth postseason-less season in the last six years. He can't fix a glaring hole in his resume if he can't even get there.Can Lamar Jackson continue his individual greatness?The quick answer is "yes." It might just look a little different.The first order of business, assuming this season is over for all intents and purposes, will be Jackson's contract. Former NFL agent Joel Corry dove into that recently. Of note ...Jackson is in the fourth year of a five-year extension that includes a no-trade clause and a clause that prevents him from being tagged after the deal expires.The Ravens have an NFL-high $366.74 million in 2027 cap commitments.Jackson has an $84.34 million cap hit next year, a number that absolutely must come down via extension if the Ravens wish to keep him.Baltimore should absolutely want to keep Jackson, even with the injury history. Through three games this year, he led the league in yards per attempt and was on pace for his highest missed-tackle rate and highest yards per rush of his career, all while not running as much as earlier in his career.They have also been truly unlucky with injuries. He was healthy in 2023 and 2024. Last year's hamstring and this year's ankle were unfortunate, but the thumb was a freak injury. Perhaps we should expect him to miss a few games every year from now on, but there's also a reasonable chance he doesn't.Jackson will be 30 next year, but 30 is not ancient. John Elway won his first Super Bowl at 37. Matthew Stafford got his first at 34. Drew Brees was 31. Peyton Manning was 30.Josh Allen is 30 and, like Jackson, hasn't been to a Super Bowl. Joe Burrow is about a month older than Jackson and hasn't won one.A common budding misconception is that Jackson can't be a star as he gets older and he runs less and/or less effectively. But Jackson has proved to be a superb pocket quarterback. His development as a passer is as impressive as it gets. Since 2023, Jackson has the third-highest yards per attempt in the NFL on throws inside the pocket and released within three seconds -- aka without much improvisation going on.Jackson may never reach the heights he was on the path to after being on the precipice of becoming the youngest three-time MVP ever in 2024. That's the sad truth about a player playing hurt and/or missing significant chunks of three years of his prime. Would he have another MVP? Two? A Super Bowl ring? We'll never know, and that's tough to swallow.But there's a version of Jackson -- a little luckier, a little better in the playoffs, a lot better of a passer than he was his younger years -- that can still be a superstar for many years and get him back on a path that ends with him as an all-time great.

        MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- Two weeks ago this morning, just before Memphis opened against Iowa State, KenPom.com projected the Tigers to finish with a lower point total than their opponents in each of their first four games. In other words, a 0-4 start seemed possible, if not likely. And once you consider that this is the same program that started 26-0 in 2008, has appeared in three Final Fours under three different coaches, and has produced a No. 1 pick in the NBA Draft, you can start to understand why folks down here, where I grew up and still live, had largely clocked out after the worst season in 56 years, evidence being season-ticket numbers hard to believe.But none of that mattered Sunday.Because, on Sunday inside FedExForum, where Memphis and Louisville once played a conference tournament championship game so memorable that, believe it or not, an iconic rock band wrote a song about it, the two programs got back together -- and not with the Tigers off to that predicted 0-3 start but, rather, with the Tigers sitting at 2-1 with victories over Iowa State and VCU and the lone loss coming at Vanderbilt.Nobody had a better first week of the season than Memphis. That was true last Sunday. Now, on this Monday, you can also say that nobody has had a more surprising first two weeks of the season than Memphis, especially after the Tigers came from 18 down to beat Louisville 98-78 and improve to 3-1."Last year was an anomaly," Hardaway said following the win. "To me, that's a one-off, bro. It's over. My teams don't play like that."This one certainly does not, which is why the city is reconnecting with it. And I can write that with confidence because, again, I grew up here, still live here, graduated from the university and was the program's beat writer for four years before moving to CBS Sports. Trust me when I tell you, things have slipped, and it was reasonable to wonder if it was recoverable with the Tigers stuck in what rates as the sport's ninth-best conference, a league with no programs that seem comparable in either history or ambition.
Anybody who reads the Top 25 And 1 regularly knows Memphis hasn't been in it as much as it used to be. The general lack of success relative to all normal historical standards, including zero trips to the Sweet 16 since 2009, has taken a toll on the fanbase.But none of that mattered Sunday.Because, on Sunday, it looked like a decent percentage of the people who used to care deeply about the Tigers decided to head downtown and reminisce a little bit thanks to Hardaway building a roster that seems fun and was off to a 2-1 start. Now it's 3-1 with three victories over schools ranked in the top 60 at KenPom. It's a strong resume for the American Athletic Conference favorites and the reason Memphis is No. 25 in Monday morning's updated CBS Sports Top 25 And 1 daily college basketball rankings.For whatever it's worth, KenPom is now projecting Memphis to finish 14-4 in the American and win the league by multiple games. If that's the way things unfold, it'll be a job well done by Hardaway, who all along insisted that if he were given a ninth year at his alma mater, he'd get things back on track.

title: Iowa State women's basketball coach suspended for making 'inappropriate contact' with player during huddle - CBS Sports
description: Bill Fennelly, who has been ISU's coach since 1995 and is planning to retire at the end of the season, will serve
body:
Bill Fennelly, who has been ISU's coach since 1995 and is planning to retire at the end of the season, will serve the suspension Wednesday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:17 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Iowa State women's basketball coach Bill Fennelly has been suspended one game for making "inappropriate contact" with guard Sienna Harvey during a timeout late in the Cyclones' 69-64 win over UIC on Sunday. Fennelly will serve his suspension on Wednesday when Iowa State plays Northern Iowa. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will serve as acting head coach for that game. "We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not," Iowa State director of athletics Jared Benko said in a statement. "We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes, and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions."With just over two minutes to play in Iowa State's win over UIC, Fennelly got animated while talking to his players during a timeout. At one point, he got in Harvey's face, put his hand on the top of her head and gave her a slight push. 
"I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game," Fennelly said in a statement. "I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward."Fennelly has been the head coach at Iowa State since 1995, and has turned the Cyclones into one of the most consistent programs in the country. Prior to his arrival, Iowa State had never made the NCAA Tournament; in his 31 seasons in charge, they have made 24 appearances, including six Sweet Sixteens and two Elite Eights. Iowa State lost nine players to the transfer portal after last season, however, including Audi Crooks, Addy Brown, Jada Williams and Kenzie Hare, and Fennelly announced in October that he will retire at the end of this season. 
"While I still love coaching and am working as hard as ever, I understand that this job has an expiration date. After talking with my family, I have made the decision that the 2026-27 season will be my last," Fennelly said at the time. "Announcing my intention now is what is best for everyone in our program and provides the new athletics director clarity on my future and allows them to make plans for the program moving forward."

title: 10 most interesting MLB non-tender decisions, including a Red Sox staple and a former Rookie of the Year - CBS Sports
description: Teams must tender contracts to arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players by Friday, Nov. 20, at 5 p.m.
body:
Teams must tender contracts to arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players by Friday, Nov. 20, at 5 p.m.
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:15 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        This Friday, Nov. 20, is an important date on MLB's offseason calendar. It is the deadline for teams to offer 2027 contracts to their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players. The player does not have to sign by Friday's 5 p.m. ET deadline, but he must be offered a contract. If he's not, the player is considered non-tendered and immediately becomes a free agent.   Dozens of players are non-tendered every offseason when teams determine their production no longer warrants the salary. Adolis García, Nathaniel Lowe, Alek Manoah, and Christopher Morel were among the notable non-tenders last offseason. Go back a few years and big names like Cody Bellinger and Kyle Schwarber were non-tendered.   With that in mind, here are the 10 most interesting non-tender decisions ahead of Friday's deadline, using the arbitration salary projections at the indispensable MLB Trade Rumors. You can be sure these teams will scour the trade market for these players and try to get something back before making the non-tender official.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       1. Jarren Duran, OF, Red Sox   
Projected salary: $11.1 million (team control through 2028)   Duran was a non-tender candidate even before the Jake Bauers signing pushed him out of the everyday lineup. There is no such thing as too many good players, but the Red Sox now have two first basemen (Bauers and Willson Contreras) and four outfielders (Duran, Wilyer Abreu, Roman Anthony, Ceddanne Rafaela). Mickey Gasper and Masataka Yoshida are still around too. That's eight players for five lineup spots (first base, DH, three outfield spots). On any given day, three of those guys will be on the bench. Duran, who got MVP votes in 2024, had a 20-20 season in 2026, but it came with a ballooning strikeout rate and a .266 on-base percentage. He has been on the trade block for close to two years now and the writing is on the wall. If the Red Sox are unable to trade Duran this week, there's a real chance he'll get non-tendered Friday given his hefty salary projection.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
       2. Spencer Torkelson, 1B, Tigers   
Projected salary: $7.7 million (team control through 2028)   Former No. 1 overall draft picks have been non-tendered in the past (Tim Beckham most recently), just not by the team that drafted them. Non-tendering Torkelson would be a tough look for the Tigers even though he has not developed into the impact hitter he was projected to be coming out of Arizona State. Simply put, the salary is beginning to outweigh the production. Torkelson, 27, is a 25-30 homer bat with one of the league's highest strikeout rates, middling on-base percentages, and no secondary value (defense, baserunning, etc.). That said, the Tigers do not have an obvious replacement first baseman ready to step in (Colt Keith was the backup in 2026). That, plus the fact that Torkelson has No. 1 pick pedigree, could keep him in Detroit another year.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       3. Luis Gil, RHP, Yankees   
Projected salary: $2.3 million (team control through 2029)   The American League Rookie of the Year in 2024, Gil has battled injuries and ineffectiveness in the two seasons since. The swing-and-miss rate on his fastball went from an elite 28.5% in 2024 to a below-average 18.8% in 2025 and 17.4% in 2026. Gil, 28, spent time in Triple-A this past season and the Yankees moved him into the bullpen late in the year, where the results were so-so. The salary projection is a pittance, particularly for a team with New York's payroll, though Gil is now out of minor-league options (he must pass through waivers to go to Triple-A) and doesn't have an obvious role. Because he is a pitcher and breathing, and also has a major award win in the not-too-distant past, the Yankees might be able to find a trade partner this week. If not, Gil is a definite non-tender candidate.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       4. Ernie Clement, 2B, Blue Jays   
Projected salary: $7.6 million (team control through 2028)   A fan favorite and an All-Star this past season, Clement crashed hard in the second half, and the fact of the matter is he has a .295 on-base percentage in his three full seasons with the Blue Jays. Also, the soon-to-be 31-year-old's defensive numbers tumbled this year. Clement's contact skills are elite and he's a versatile, high-energy player. As a utility guy, he's an ace. As an everyday player, he's stretched. Clement's projected salary is hefty for a utility player, particularly one with limited offensive upside who no longer reliably catches the baseball. My guess is the Blue Jays will keep him and live with the salary, but it's not an obvious decision.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
       5. Royce Lewis, 1B, Twins   
Projected salary: $5.1 million (team control through 2028)   Similar to Torkelson, non-tendering a former No. 1 overall pick would be a tough look for the Twins, but a clean break might be best for all involved at this point. Lewis, 27, has trended down since his boffo second half in 2023, enough that he was sent to Triple-A for a spell this summer. He's also moved down the defensive spectrum from third base to first base. It's not due to a lack of effort; Lewis is a major tinkerer who has tried all sorts of swing adjustments. It just hasn't come together. A fresh start elsewhere, away from the spotlight of former No. 1 pick and face of the franchise, might be best for him. The budget-conscious Twins could then reallocate the projected $5.1 million elsewhere on the roster. Right now, they can't count on Lewis to hit or have a meaningful impact defensively.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       6. Nolan Gorman, 3B, Cardinals   
Projected salary: $3.4 million (team control through 2028)   In 2023, Gorman slugged 27 home runs and looked like one of baseball's top young power hitters. In the three seasons since, he has not come close to repeating that success. The hope was that moving him to third base, his natural position, would unlock Gorman's offense following the Nolan Arenado trade. That didn't happen, and Gorman spent a big chunk of the summer in Triple-A, where he continued to have a hard time making contact. Now 26, Gorman has a minor-league option remaining and can go to Triple-A again in 2027, but the signs are not subtle. The Cardinals are reportedly seeking a stopgap third baseman until top prospect Jesús Báez is ready, which would likely not be the case if they had any belief in Gorman. That projected $3.4 million salary is a high price for a reclamation project ticketed for the minors.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       7. Jake Burger, 1B, Rangers   
Projected salary: $6.9 million (team control through 2028)   Right-handed power is in short supply throughout baseball and Burger, 31 in April, has hit at least 28 home runs in three of the last four years. He is a one-tool player, though. The home runs come with low batting averages, low on-base percentages, higher-than-average strikeout rates, and little to no defensive or baserunning value. Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young said his team lacked "grit and toughness," whatever that means, and indicated he wants more hitters who grind out at-bats. That's not Burger, who can hit the ball a mile but is not known for making life tough on pitchers. The $6.9 million projection could be deemed too pricey for a player with such a limited skill set.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
       8. Camilo Doval, RHP, Giants   
Projected salary: $6.6 million (team control through 2027)   Doval went from the Yankees to the Pirates at the trade deadline, then from the Pirates to the Giants on waivers in September. He's a former All-Star who led the National League in saves in 2023, two things that have boosted his arbitration salaries. Since 2023, Doval has been a middle reliever who was on the outside of the Circle of Trust™ more often than not. The 29-year-old righty still throws very hard. There's nothing wrong with his arm. It's hard to believe he gets hit as hard as he does sometimes. Doval earned $6.1 million in 2026 and a player cannot have a salary cut by more than 20% during his team control years. That would set Doval's minimum 2027 salary at $4.88 million. I wonder if the Giants would offer him a pay cut, say $5.5M or so, and tell him it's either that or a non-tender. That happens a few times a year around the league.
                            
    
                                                
                    
       9. Gavin Sheets, 1B/OF, Padres   
Projected salary: $6.5 million (team control through 2027)   A fan favorite in San Diego -- "Ho-ly Sheets!" chants are commonplace during his at-bats at Petco Park -- Sheets has fallen by the wayside a bit with the Padres, so much so that he started just one of their six postseason games this year. The 30-year-old is a platoon player who is good against righties more than great and is a defensive liability at both first base and left field. Realistically, Sheets is a platoon DH, and teams rarely pay well for that role unless they're confident they will get big offensive numbers. In the grand scheme of things, the projected $6.5 million isn't much. It is top-of-the-market dollars for this skill set, however.    
                            
    
                                                
                    
       10. Ronel Blanco, RHP, Astros   
Projected salary: $1.4 million (team control through 2029)   Two years ago, Blanco threw a no-hitter in his eighth career start. This year, he was so far out of the picture that he pitched once in Houston's last 12 games (two innings at the end of a 13-2 blowout), and the Astros opted to start Peter Lambert on two days' rest with a postseason spot on the line in Game 162. Blanco, who is older than you may realize (he turned 33 in August), returned from Tommy John surgery this summer and had a rough go of it. The pitching-needy Astros could send him to Triple-A next season, as he has a minor-league option remaining, but his stuff was diminished after surgery, and again, they didn't trust him late in the year. You would be surprised at how many cheap pitchers get non-tendered every year. Blanco could join them this week.

title: 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame ballot released: 8 things to know, including newcomers, trends and a prediction - CBS Sports
description: Buster Posey, Jon Lester and more join a ballot that still includes Alex Rodríguez, Chase Utley and other holdove
body:
Buster Posey, Jon Lester and more join a ballot that still includes Alex Rodríguez, Chase Utley and other holdovers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The ballot for the BBWAA portion of the 2027 Baseball Hall of Fame vote was revealed on Monday, featuring 13 holdovers and 14 newcomers. The full ballot, in alphabetical order, is Bobby Abreu, Jake Arrieta, Jay Bruce, Mark Buehrle, Asdrúbal Cabrera, Starlin Castro, Wade Davis, Brett Gardner, Cole Hamels, Félix Hernández, Torii Hunter, Jon Lester, Andrew Miller, Dustin Pedroia, Andy Pettitte, Buster Posey, Alex Rodriguez, Francisco Rodríguez, Jimmy Rollins, Pablo Sandoval, Ervin Santana, Kyle Seager, Joakim Soria, Chase Utley, Omar Vizquel, David Wright and Ryan Zimmerman. Newcomers to the ballot are in bold.As a reminder, players must receive votes on at least 75% of the ballots cast to be inducted into the Hall of Fame with the 2027 class. Those who get at least 5% of the vote can remain on the ballot the following year, and so on, for a maximum of 10 voting cycles. Players who are on the ballot for 10 years without getting 75% of the vote, in addition to players not getting 5% of the vote, fall off the ballot in ensuing years, though that doesn't mean the doors to the Hall are permanently shut. The results will be announced on Jan. 19, with the induction set for Cooperstown over the summer.
Here's everything else you need to know about the Baseball Hall of Fame this offseason. 1. This isn't the only Hall of Fame vote this offseasonAs alluded to earlier, there are two different votes each offseason. The BBWAA vote is for former players who have been retired from Major League Baseball for at least five years. It's the most common method in mainstream Hall of Fame ballot discussions. When you hear stuff like "first-ballot Hall of Famer," it means via the BBWAA vote. Players who don't make it via the BBWAA vote can get extra chances via committees. That's how, for example, Jeff Kent made it last year. Formerly called the Veterans Committee, the Hall of Fame now uses Era Committees, which are divided into two categories: contemporary baseball (1980 to present) and classic (prior to 1980). The contemporary ballot is then split into two, one for players and one for non-players like umpires, executives, pioneers and managers. 
Sure enough, this time around, it is a non-player Contemporary Baseball Committee, which looks at "managers, umpires and executives whose most significant career impact was realized since 1980."It's a strong group: Sandy AldersonDusty BakerBruce BochyJoe MaddonLou PiniellaBrian SabeanTed TurnerBill WhiteWe'll dive further into this group as we get closer to the Dec. 6 vote. 2. There is probably one first-ballot Hall of FamerGiants legend Buster Posey joins the ballot, and he's one of those cases where I don't think a bunch of people need to delve deeply into his numbers. More than statistics, sometimes we get "feel" guys, as in, you just know he's a Hall of Famer. Posey qualifies there, I would think, for 75% of the electorate. We'll obviously do a deeper dive in the coming weeks, but even without the longevity component (Posey only played in parts of 12 MLB seasons), I think he's in. As for the rest of the first-timers, the best case would be Jon Lester. Given the way a lot of similar starting pitchers have been treated in voting in recent years, my hunch is he'll be able to hang around on the ballot, but he has a major uphill battle in order to get in. 
Then you're looking at Brett Gardner, Ryan Zimmerman, Kyle Seager, the short peak of Jake Arrieta and relief work of Andrew Miller. Good players worth mentioning, of course, but they won't sniff the Hall and it seems likely all behind Posey and Lester are one-and-dones on this ballot, as they'll fall short of 5% of the vote. 3. A-Rod playing out the string?This is the sixth year for Alex Rodriguez on the ballot, which means it's the sixth time that I point out that we don't really need much time to go over his case. His numbers say he's one of the 10 best position players of all time, but his ties to PEDs are keeping him out to this point. He did rise from 37.1% of the vote in 2025 to 40% last time, a new high-water mark. The progress is too modest to believe it's trending toward him getting in, but the number this year is certainly worth watching. If he somehow makes a leap to the 50% range, a deeper conversation might be in order.
4. Utley's big chance? While some voters don't mind sending in blank ballots to prove some sort of nebulous point, most impose limits on themselves. Whether it's the actual rule of 10 or some voters saying they'll only vote, for example, for a maximum of three players on any given ballot, relatively weak ballots can leave openings for the best players to show huge gains. With Carlos Beltràn and Andruw Jones getting in last year and only one strong first-year candidate, perhaps Chase Utley can benefit. Utley is only in his fourth year on the ballot, but he's already made significant gains: First year: 28.8%Second: 39.8%Third: 59.1%He only needs to add 15.9 points after jumping nearly 20 last voting cycle. The situation is ripe for Utley to either get all the way in or get close enough to where he probably makes the Hall of Fame in 2028. 
5. Watch those starting pitchersSome of us are pushing to lower the Hall of Fame standard on modern starting pitchers, given the decreases in workload and how it affects their career numbers. We might be making some headway, but it's still tough sledding. Here are the holdover starting pitchers and their standing: Andy Pettitte got 48.5% of the vote in his eighth try last cycle. He started out at 9.9% and jumped more than 20 points last time around, but he still has a long way to go. Félix Hernández might be trending toward induction. He got 20.6% of the vote in his first year and jumped to 46.1% last year, his second ballot. Another big jump here and he has a real shot. Will Cole Hamels have a similar leap? He got 23.8% of the vote last year, his first on the ballot. Mark Buehrle was in ballot purgatory before last year, getting between 5.8% and 11.4% of the vote for his first five cycles, but he shot up to 20% last year. This is his seventh ballot and he'd need another major move to have realistic hope. 6. K-Rod and how it could relate moving forwardThe bar for relievers to make the Hall of Fame is justly pretty high. We recently saw Billy Wagner make a late move and make it in his last try on the BBWAA ballot. Francisco Rodríguez has had four chances on the ballot and gotten between 7.8% and 11.8% of the vote thus far. K-Rod ranks sixth all time in saves and has good rate stats. He's worth tracking as it relates to three active relievers. Kenley Jansen is third in saves with a similar number of innings pitched to K-Rod. Craig Kimbrel is fifth and has more than 100 fewer innings pitched. Aroldis Chapman is ninth and in the ballpark of Kimbrel in workload to this point. 
If K-Rod continues to have trouble making headway toward induction, does that mean Kimbrel and Chapman will have trouble as well? What about Jansen? 7. Tracking the other holdoversWho else is back on the ballot? A quick look: Bobby Abreu, who got 30.8% of the vote last year in his seventh try. Jimmy Rollins got 25.4% on his fifth ballot last cycle. Dustin Pedroia received 20.7% last year and it was his second ballot. Omar Vizquel is playing out the string at this point. His tally dwindled to 18.4% last year and this is now his 10th and final ballot. David Wright got 14.8% of the vote last year, his third ballot. Torii Hunter continues to linger just north of the 5% threshold. He got 8.7% last year in his sixth try.8. PredictionPosey is a lock. If the committee era chooses Bochy, Baker and/or Sabean, that would be some nice San Francisco flavor, too, right? I'll predict that committee ballot at a later date, though. I'll also say Utley's good roll here continues with a relatively weak ballot (at least when you factor in what the PED stain has done to some guys).   
On the player side, my 2027 Hall of Fame class prediction is Buster Posey and Chase Utley.

title: Projecting every SEC starting quarterback for the 2027 college football season - CBS Sports
description: College football's transfer portal opens Jan. 4 and within the SEC, several teams could be looking for new blood ahead of the 2027 seaso
body:
College football's transfer portal opens Jan. 4 and within the SEC, several teams could be looking for new blood ahead of the 2027 season.This could be one of the weaker quarterback markets in the transfer portal that we've seen in recent years, but much of that won't be known until mid-December when exit meetings are completed and players make their respective moves. That means teams taking expensive chances on incoming talent or deciding their current situation might be the best move going forward.Betting on the future is costly and we've already seen how pricey it is to retain elite-tier quarterbacks with star power (ask Mississippi State). For several potential signal-callers entering the portal, 2027 NFL Draft grades will play a pivotal role in decisions.The job of a general manager within the SEC is not a fun role and this is where numbered heads together in roster discussions hits a fever pitch when the regular season ends. We're doing the unthinkable here and trying to project next season's starting quarterbacks in the SEC for every team 10 months out. Hat tip to several industry insiders at 247Sports who proved to be invaluable sounding boards. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    AlabamaProjected 2027 starter: Keelon RussellThe sophomore from Duncanville, Texas has run away with the job this season with impressive fluidity as a passer with enough mobility to keep defenses honest in Ryan Grubb's offense under Kalen DeBoer. Since the Crimson Tide's loss at Tennessee last month, Russell's thrown nine touchdown passes with two interceptions over Alabama's last three games -- all SEC wins -- and is now responsible for 26 total scores this season. He has first-round ability if his development continues at a program best-suited to flex his full repertoire.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    ArkansasProjected 2027 starter: TransferThere are doubts Arkansas will hitch its wagon to KJ Jackson again after watching him stumble to a 4-6 record this season with a significant sample. Quarterback play is far from the Razorbacks' biggest concern this offseason, but it is something Ryan Silverfield and the Razorbacks' coaching staff must get this right in January. 
Arkansas should be one of several SEC programs shopping for a new starter. It would benefit the Razorbacks to land a veteran who can handle pressure, hit throws downfield and most importantly, operate efficiently. Year 2 is when fans need to see the offense take shape and Jackson's best outing coming in Week 11 against South Carolina is simply too late to reverse season-long opinions.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    AuburnProjected 2027 starter: TransferIt's no secret the Tigers will go big-game hunting this cycle. Like most teams, however, Auburn's focus is fixing its offensive line before anything works for Alex Golesh. They're going to take a "fresh" approach under center according to one insider connected with the program since there's no plug-and-play option currently on the roster. Tristan Ti'a, a transfer from Oregon State, has more eligibility and is expected to return after backup up Byrum Brown this season, but his reps are limited. The Tigers need a quarterback who can process quickly and get the ball out given Golesh's scheme. Auburn's bowl-eligible for the first time in three seasons, which is a net positive for a first-year staff, but there are questions about this roster in 2027 that must be answered to continue a step ladder-like trajectory. Three-star prospect Gary Chatman will sign next month, but likely won't see the field during his campaign.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    FloridaProjected 2027 starter: Aaron PhiloRather than rip the offense from the studs in January with a transfer, one insider said it's "50-50" right now on Florida's ultimate plan, pointing to an offense line rebuild being the bigger priority on that side of the football. That's where much of the Gators' offseason spending offensively will be, at least that's the expectation in mid-November for a team that's been on-again, off-again in Jon Sumrall's first campaign. Offseason transfer Aaron Philo helped Florida get off to a 4-0 start before an injury hampered his progress and led to Tramell Jones providing a spark off the bench. Jones helped the Gators to a win at nationally-ranked Texas before fumbling away his second career start Nov. 7 against Oklahoma with multiple turnovers. Philo, who returned to his starting role against Georgia before throwing two interceptions in the first half last month, was tapped by offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner given the Georgia Tech connection and there's a sense the Gators will give that marriage another try next spring. All bets are off if neither player separates themselves from the other the rest of the way, however.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    GeorgiaProjected 2027 starter: Ryan PuglisiUnless the Bulldogs get into the transfer fray and decide to buck tradition under Kirby Smart and pay up for a newcomer, the time has come for Puglisi to take over as QB1 in Athens. 
The former four-star signee in the 2024 class has been developed in Mike Bobo's system for three years, spending this season as Gunner Stockton's backup after redshirting as a freshman then appearing in seven games last fall. The Bulldogs should feel confident he can operate this offense moving forward as Stockton departs having exhausted his eligibility. Going to the portal would mean Georgia's outing for someone who can come in for QB1 reps and Smart hasn't done that since signing JT Daniels and Jamie Newman the same cycle in 2020. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    KentuckyProjected 2027 starter: Kenny MincheyWhile his first season with the Wildcats isn't ending the way he would've liked, Minchey's been an ideal distributor in Joe Sloan's offense and leader for first-year coach Will Stein at Kentucky. 
Consecutive losses in November derailed this team's CFP path, but Minchey's decision-making remains elite and simply needs more help The former Notre Dame transfer has thrown for 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns and two interceptions in 10 starts and will be one of the league's top retuning players at his position in the spring.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    LSUProjected 2027 starter: Sam LeavittThis was perhaps the toughest call on the list, especially in light of Leavitt again turning the ball over in the red zone multiple times in a showcase game. But I ask whether it's worth blowing everything up offensively and going back to the portal for another quarterback? Both parties need to be in agreement here. That's how one source put it when asked about how Lane Kiffin will play his quarterback hand this offseason prior to Saturday night's loss to Texas. The Tigers fell short of CFP expectations with its transfer signal caller, who made critical error after critical error in high-pressure situations against some of the top teams on the schedule. LSU knew Leavitt's gunslinger-like play, however, and that's part of what makes him unique. 
For Kiffin's system to work, Leavitt will need to play a more controlled style as a passer in 2027 and most of all, be a bit more confident from the pocket. He took too many shots to the body this fall, evidenced by 337 yards rushing on 98 carries (3.4 YPC) and eight touchdowns. Landen Clark and Husan Longstreet could return, too, and top-100 recruit Peyton Houston is expected to sign next month.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Mississippi StateProjected 2027 starter: Kamario TaylorHow impactful was Super Kamario on the Bulldogs' season? Mississippi State was 4-0 in games he started this fall prior to a 56-23 setback against Alabama on Oct. 3 that started off a significant turf toe situation for its start quarterback. That was the first of six consecutive losses heading into Saturday's home bout with Tennessee Tech and explains why Taylor's returning on an eye-watering deal in excess of $6 million. Prior to suffering what resulted in a season-ending injury against the Crimson Tide, Taylor was on a record-setting pace in Starkville as one of the Heisman frontrunners. He's more important to the program's success than coach Jeff Lebby and that's not something muttered lightly. Lebby's 11-24 with the Bulldogs entering Week 12 and understands his future is directly tied to Mississippi State's success in 2027 with Taylor running the show. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    MissouriProjected 2027 starter: Austin SimmonsOne of several signal-callers to officially put the retention pen to paper this season, Simmons will be back for the Tigers after a notable first campaign at Missouri. Simmons is tied for the SEC lead with 21 touchdown passes. "Any time you can return a quarterback in this league, that's a huge deal," Drinkwitz said earlier this moth. "In this day and age, you have to have a quarterback. ... The teams in contention for the SEC Championships and College Football Playoff, most have a returning starting quarterbacks, or at least a quarterback that's been in their system because those reps add up. For us, we'll be in that mold next year."
                            
    
                                                
                    
    OklahomaProjected 2027 starter: TransferWill Jason Witten have the interim OC tag removed and be the guy calling plays next season for the Sooners? If that happens, Witten would've convincing general manager Jim Nagy and coach Brent Venables there's a quarterback in the market that would fit what he wants to run in Norman. 
After grabbing John Mateer and former play-caller Ben Arbuckle from the Group of Six two cycles ago, there's always the package deal route again if Nagy/Venables believe it can work. The most important aspect of Oklahoma's quarterback situation is that Venables must be hands-off during the season so he can focus on the programs bread and butter -- his side of the football. Look for a Group of Six proven threat in the portal to land at Oklahoma, one who must work out for Venables -- or else.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Ole MissProjected 2027 starter: Deuce KnightThis could go one of two ways for the Rebels. Those close to the program say there's a surge of momentum behind Knight, the former Auburn transfer who is playing behind Trinidad Chambliss this season -- or Ole Miss may choose to jump in the portal sweepstakes for one of the bigger guns available this portal cycle. Much of that depends on who's out there and schematic fit with offensive coordinator John David Baker. One insider said there's growing confidence that 2027 commit Keegan Croucher is going to find his way to the field sooner rather than later in Oxford, promising given the legacy and production void Chambliss leaves after finishing his career this month against Mississippi State and bowl season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    South CarolinaProjected 2027 starter: LaNorris SellersA first-round NFL Draft grade might be the only thing that gets LaNorris Sellers out of Columbia after this season. Multiple sources told CBS Sports earlier this month that South Carolina and Sellers' camp have opened conversations about a return in 2027, and there's plenty of reason for both sides to see where those talks go as long as OC Kendal Briles stays put.Then there's his brother, Jayden Sellers, who returns from a season-ending knee injury. The chance to play alongside him on offense carries weight, especially after the injury cut into their time on the field together.If Sellers gets a first-round grade at season's end, he's not expected to come back. In the event Sellers does turn pro, the Gamecocks could be another team fishing for a transfer since backup Cutter Woods doesn't appear to be a natural fit in Briles' offense. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TennesseeProjected 2027 starter: George MacIntyreJosh Heupel's top quarterbacks in Knoxville have all been transfers, but the Vols' coaching staff was hoping that going young at the position this season with the combination of top-flight Faizon Brandon and George MacIntyre would establish long-term continuity under center. One insider characterized the situation at Tennessee with "multiple layers" and said "all options" are on the table following Brandon's injury and ultimate benching this season, though he came in relief of an injured MacIntyre in Saturday's road win at Texas A&M. The five-star freshman was supposed to be the future of the program, but it's been MacIntyre who has shown more consistency and ability to operate the offense. How MacIntyre performs against LSU, Vanderbilt and potentially in the College Football Playoff will go a long way in determining Tennessee's quarterback moves this cycle. Brandon wants to start and the Vols are trying to keep him engaged. Could Tennessee go after an immediate transfer replacement to top the depth chart in January? Will the Vols enter spring practice with another Brandon vs. MacIntyre competition? This is one of the hardest projections to make in the conference and it may depend on who's out there for the taking in the portal.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TexasProjected 2027 starter: KJ LaceyThe tentative expectation inside the program at Texas is Arch Manning turning pro after the College Football Playoff this season, leaving the Longhorns with this ready-to-step-up sophomore as the next option. There was talk earlier this fall of Steve Sarkisian potentially going with Lacey if Manning's inconsistency lingered, but Manning has mostly picked it up down the stretch and is playing at a top-end level late in games. Lacey has made three appearances this season as a former four-star recruit in the 2025 cycle out of Alabama and has seen his share of quality reps during practice as the team's primary No. 2. Next season will be his third in Sarkisian's scheme and he should be comfortable as a probable first-time starter in September.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Texas A&MProjected 2027 starter: TransferThe ship has sailed on Marcel Reed as Texas A&M's starter in 2027. After a tumultuous season offensively, what exactly would Mike Elko be buying with another year of this same quarterback and play-caller combination? The pairing with Holmon Wiggins hasn't worked and the Aggies' place near the bottom of the SEC in several offensive categories makes it a tough sell on convincing the fan base to prepare for Year 3 of Reed as QB1 in College Station.Texas A&M needs a quarterback who can keep the offense on schedule and make defenses pay as a passer, especially on third down. The Aggies have the resources to land one of the top quarterbacks in this portal cycle. With that kind of spending power, Elko should have his pick of several proven starters.And about that -- who calls plays for the next guy? This decision might be more important than who's playing quarterback. Elko's loyalty to Wiggins could buy his coordinator another season, but if you're investing in a new quarterback, this is the time to decide who gives him the best chance to win at an elite level.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    VanderbiltProjected 2027 starter: Jared CurtisGrowing pains were expected for the five-star freshman this season and Curtis only has four touchdown passes with six interceptions in six starts against SEC competition. However, he's shown enough flashes to suggest the program's heavy investment in him was warranted and there's optimism that next season -- with another full offseason of schematic mastery under his belt -- that the Commodores can get back to bowl eligibility under Clark Lea. Building around Curtis and strengthening the offensive front are priorities in the transfer portal this cycle.

Eason couldn't take the credit for his season high in scoring, instead giving that credit to Houston's opponent

        The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night. While Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench. That 25-point performance represents a new season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently. "Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason said.  
A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington. The Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.
Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

        The dust is settling in the College Football Playoff picture with two games left in the regular season before conference championship weekend.For this exercise, we're taking the teams at the back end of the CFP Selection Committee's second rankings who did not lose in Week 11. For the teams who did — like Houston, Kentucky, USC and others — we're expecting noticeable tumbles outside of the bubble.After Oklahoma's win over Ole Miss on Sunday ended the Rebels' faint hopes of reaching the 12-team bracket, we believe only six teams are competing for virtually the final two spots in the at-large rankings. The rest of the 10 spots will be filled as follows, according to our latest projection, in no particular order: Georgia, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee (SEC); Miami (ACC); Notre Dame; Boise State (Group of Six); UCLA and Indiana (Big Ten); Utah (Big 12).Some of this could change quickly if current favorites fail to handle their business over the next two weekends, but various analytics models point to this half-dozen still being in the discussion.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 BYU (8-2)Best-case scenario: Win out + Texas Tech fails to win Big 12 and leap Cougars at 11-2 overallFollowing 11th-ranked Kentucky's loss at Florida on Saturday night, BYU and Texas Tech will be in the same cluster once again in the updated rankings — which could spell doom for BYU if the selection committee upgrades the Red Raiders for beating previously ranked Oklahoma State. BYU's win over Notre Dame is still one of college football's best of the season, but there's no meat left on the bone for the Cougars with remaining matchups against Kansas and Cincinnati.Updated CBS Sports projection: First team out at No. 12
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Texas Tech (9-1)Best-case scenario: Win out + capture Big 12 ChampionshipOne of only two bubble teams in control of their destiny, the Red Raiders can make it easy by seizing an auto-berth in the bracket with three more victories. Saturday's win in Stillwater was the first step toward getting back to the title game down the stretch with Baylor and TCU left to play. Over his last three starts, Thomas Castellanos has accumulated 1,026 yards of total offense with 12 touchdowns.
Updated CBS Sports projection: No. 11 seed as last team in
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 Wake Forest (9-1)Best-case scenario: Win out + capture ACC ChampionshipJake Dickert and the Demon Deacons are making sure they're leaving no stone unturned in front of the committee with this blitzkrieg of success in the ACC since the early-season loss to Miami. If style points matter, Wake Forest has aced that test during this seven-game winning streak. This squad hasn't allowed a first-half point since mid-October, and Gio Lopez has produced eye-popping numbers over nine starts — 19 touchdown passes, one interception and eight rushing scores.Updated CBS Sports projection: No. 10 seed
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 15 Iowa (8-2)Best-case scenario: Win out + capture Big Ten ChampionshipSeveral metrics are working against the Hawkeyes right now, including the lack of a nationally ranked win, but they do only have two losses. Entering Week 12, Kirk Ferentz's squad has posted three victories over teams with winning records and gets two more chances to add to that against Illinois and Nebraska. Should Iowa and Oregon win out, we project the Ducks to jump the Hawkeyes despite not matching records. That's due to Oregon's heavy advantage in strength of schedule and other factors.Updated CBS Sports projection: No CFP bid
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 16 Oregon (7-3)Best-case scenario: Win out + capture Big Ten ChampionshipOregon has looked the part in recent weeks on a three-game winning streak and has the best resume of all current three-loss hopefuls rounding out the discussion. The Ducks have five wins over teams with winning records, including three who are currently ranked and seem to have figured it out offensively with Dylan Raiola at quarterback. Michigan State and Washington remain, but Oregon needs assistance from others around the Power Four to have a legitimate argument for inclusion on Selection Sunday.
Updated CBS Sports projection: No CFP bid
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 20 Ohio State (7-3)Best-case scenario: Win out + Oregon, BYU, Wake Forest lose again before end of month The Buckeyes are clinging to the slightest of hopes after holding off Northwestern, but recent losses to USC and Oregon have essentially made this campaign a failure to meet sizable expectations under Ryan Day. The win at Indiana is a great one, as is the victory over Iowa, but the recent Big Ten losses to the Ducks and Trojans are likely too much to overcome unless there's more chaos in front of Ohio State the rest of the way.Updated CBS Sports projection: No CFP bid

        Hello and welcome to the last full work week before Thanksgiving. In Major League Baseball, that usually means a slow news week. Those of us wanting a flurry of moves before the CBA expires on Dec. 1 are starting to lose a little hope, but hey, it's still possible. We can start with a fresh batch of rumors and wait for something to come to fruition. As for the news and rumors for Monday, Nov. 16, let's go. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orioles interested in bringing Rogers backThe Orioles are "operating with the intent of adding" a left-handed starting pitcher, according to the Baltimore Banner. They have extended a qualifying offer to Trevor Rogers and though he's expected to decline it, a reunion remains possible. If not, the Orioles are also reportedly interested in lefty free agents Kris Bubic, Matthew Boyd and David Peterson. Rogers is the best option here. He finished last season with a 2.90 ERA in his last 20 starts. CBS Sports ranked him as the No. 3 free agent this offseason and the best non-Tarik Skubal pitcher on the market. Here's part of the write-up:Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years.As things stand, the Orioles' rotation starts with right-handers Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Cade Povich is a left-handed option, but they'd clearly like someone else who could qualify as a frontline starter from the left-handed side.
Minter with a lot of suitorsFree agent left-hander A.J. Minter is getting a lot of interest, per MLB Network. Coming off a season in which he was productive for both the Mets and Twins (in all, a 2.56 ERA, 1.05 WHIP and 41 strikeouts in 45 ⅔ innings), he's being chased by at least the Blue Jays, Nationals, Phillies, Rangers and Royals. Though he's closed on occasion, Minter has been a quality setup man for most of his 10 MLB years, especially with the Braves in the 2020-24 range. He has good playoff numbers, too, with a 2.88 ERA in 20 career postseason appearances.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Brewers trade for relieverThe Brewers have acquired right-handed reliever Ryan Walker from the Giants for two minor-league pitchers, the team announced late Sunday. Walker, 30, was up and down in his four years with the Giants, which included time as a closer. He had a 1.91 ERA, 10 saves and 2.8 WAR in 2024, but lost the job of closer during a sub-par 2025 season. Last year, he pitched to a 7.16 ERA and 1.81 WHIP in 32 ⅔ innings. 
We have plenty of examples of the Brewers buying low on a player and ending up getting the best version of him, so Walker is the latest to keep an eye on here.

        UTEP has fired coach Scotty Walden after three seasons, sources confirmed to CBS Sports' Chris Hummer. The Miners are 1-9 this season, and 6-28 in three years with Walden at the helm. Walden was one of the fastest risers in college football when he came to El Paso, an inspired hire after a series of lower-profile coaches. In 2016, Walden became the youngest coach at any level of college football (26) when he took over at East Texas Baptist. By 2020, he moved to Austin Peay, where he led the program to two conference championships. He hoped to bring his trademark energy and explosive offense to UTEP when he took the job in 2024, and his early tenure showed flashes of promise, finishing 3-5 in Conference USA. Walden consistently showed up in the community, even donating substantial portions of his salary towards revenue sharing to aid fundraising. But as the years went on, the Miners continued to regress, especially on offense. 
UTEP ranks No. 136 in total offense, sitting as one of seven programs to average fewer than 300 yards per game. They're last nationally in scoring offense and have failed to score more than 17 points in any FBS game this season. Their lone win was a 51-10 win over FCS Texas Southern. The timing is especially vital as the Miners play their first season in the Mountain West. Only interim-coached Northern Illinois, the lone winless team in college football, ranks within 15 spots of the Miners in the CBS Sports 138 rankings as the new league produced multiple postseason-caliber teams. 
Walden's buyout is reported to be more than $1 million, a significant chunk for one of the lowest-funded athletic departments in FBS. Athletic director Jim Senter will have a difficult time identifying candidates for a job that produced only one bowl trip since 2014.
